entries.warning: This pack's finding that Kansas has NO ABAWD waiver anywhere in the state (all 105 counties enforce work requirements) rests on WebSearch cross-checks, not a successful direct fetch of FNS's live FY2025-2029 quarterly waiver list (the fetch attempt timed out within this pack's window). County/statewide ABAWD waiver status is among the most volatile SNAP policy facts that exist and can change quarterly, tied to unemployment-rate redeterminations. Before telling a Kansas applicant whether ABAWD work rules currently apply anywhere in the state, re-fetch https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/abawd/waivers/2025-2029 directly and check for a Kansas-specific entry.

This pack's resource/asset-limit figures ($3,000 standard, $4,500 elderly/disabled) are WebSearch-aggregator-corroborated only, NOT grounded in a single directly-fetched, dated KEESM section the way this pack's SUA, income-limit, and deduction figures are. Several individual KEESM numbered sections in the 5000-5300 series either 404'd or did not state the dollar figure explicitly within this pack's fetch window. Before restating Kansas's asset-limit figures with full confidence, locate and fetch the current, dated KEESM resource-limit section directly (likely in the 5100-5300 range, adjacent to the fetched 5200/5430 sections).

This pack's certification-period statement (12-month default for non-elderly/non-disabled households) is a general SNAP-program inference, NOT grounded in a directly-fetched, dated KEESM certification-period section — this pack could not locate and fetch that specific section within its window. Before restating Kansas's certification-period structure (including whether Kansas has an interim/periodic-report requirement analogous to Connecticut's PRF or an ESAP-style simplified track for elderly/disabled households), locate and fetch the current KEESM certification-period section directly.

This pack found and corrected a 2022 news article claiming Kansans with drug felonies remain "banned for life" from SNAP, against this pack's own direct read of the CURRENT K.S.A. 39-709e text (a modified, assessment/treatment-conditioned opt-out, not an unconditional lifetime ban). This pack could not determine whether the 2022 article was describing a since-superseded earlier version of Kansas law or was simply imprecise. Before restating Kansas's drug-felony policy with full confidence, re-fetch K.S.A. 39-709e directly and check for any amendment since this pack's 2026-08-12 fetch date.

This repo's existing packages/snap-rules KS StatePolicy entry carries TWO inconsistent internal signals: a top-of-file comment (states.ts ~line 128) calling KS an 'archetype' with 'illustrative' SUA values, and a separate, undated in-code comment directly above the KS entry (states.ts ~lines 1037-1042) claiming the same SUA figures were 'confirmed live 2026-08-09' via KEESM §7226. This pack's own independent research (fetched 2026-08-12, three days after that claimed confirmation date) corroborates the SUA figures as accurate, but this pack did NOT modify packages/snap-rules (out of scope, corpus-only) and flags this internal inconsistency for whoever next touches that file to reconcile the 'archetype'/'illustrative' framing with the apparently-already-partially-corrected entry, rather than silently trusting either signal alone.

This pack's confirmed dollar figures (Standard Deduction $209/$209/$209/$223/$261/$299, SUA $469, LUA $345, Telephone Standard $44, capped excess shelter $744, Homeless Shelter Expense $198.99, Standard Medical Deduction $175, and the gross/net income-eligibility table by household size) are drawn from KEESM Appendix F-2, effective October 1, 2025, matching the current FFY2026 cycle (October 1, 2025 - September 30, 2026).
